findings.summary: The checkpoint-read fault reason is recorded in `checkpoint_fault_reasons` but never emitted anywhere an operator reads: unlike `probe_reasons`, which the tick copies onto `TickResult.probe_detail` (daemon.py:1015), `checkpoint_fault_reason` is exposed only as an in-process accessor and is read nowhere outside tests. Spec item 3's core safety property (an unreadable checkpoint is never treated as completed) holds, and the pre-existing fault-path reason still surfaces via `blocker_summary`, but the new checkpoint-fault tag is effectively invisible in production.

Documentation still describes the pre-E3 contract: docs/architecture.md:85 states the daemon reads terminal.json's mechanical fields (`terminal`/`rounds`/`run_id`) as its source, and scheduler/supervisor_events.py:13-17 says the E2/E3 scan 'reads the same terminal.json the tick already reads ... same file'. Both now route through the checkpoint-derived record.

Identity discrepancy between the dispatch context and the sealed artifact: the dispatch labels the product commit `work_head_commit` as ed3bf9063b8d02282bd36ba1a4a3601ea4ce3e07, but the committed implement handoff records `work_head_commit` 822bdc1364c609c8f4bf615d30e90de88e6b212f and `input_commit` 543424e3729054d8ed443929d68c5a21a9c568f7. This is consistent with ed3bf90 being the metadata-only materialization stacked on 822bdc13, so it reads as a mislabel in the dispatch text rather than an artifact defect, but it is flagged for the seal.

Scope limitation of this review, not a defect in the change: with read-only file tools I could not execute the prescribed `git diff --exit-code ed3bf90 dfb66ac -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` product-consistency check. Inspection of the worktree found no product-file divergence and only the expected RC review artifact under .dev-dispatch/, and the deterministic seal verifies the actual Git HEAD independently.
